subject: Mental Models
title: Confirmation Bias
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Confirmation Bias.

hook.text: A detective decided the butler did it, then only collected evidence supporting that theory. He missed the real killer.

buildup.text: Confirmation bias makes you seek information that agrees with you and ignore information that challenges you.

discovery.text: Peter Wason proved it in 1960. People given a number sequence only tested rules that confirmed their first guess.

twist.text: Being smart makes it worse. Intelligent people are better at constructing arguments for what they already believe.

climax.text: The antidote is actively seeking disconfirming evidence. Ask: what would prove me wrong?

punchline.text: Your brain is a yes-man. Force it to say no sometimes.

quiz.question: How does intelligence affect confirmation bias?
options: Smart people are immune to it
Smart people are better at constructing arguments for their existing beliefs
